gap: No result ChatGPT got states that refilling one night of AC use from the kit's own panels takes most of a day or more: StorageReview measured the BLUETTI Elite 300 taking 3.49 kWh to recharge after it delivered 2.67 kWh, so its 2×200 W kit needs 3,490 ÷ 400 = 8.7 hours of full-rated panel output, and the 1,200 W solar input still needs 2.9 hours.
standout_why: Compared against homepowerfacts.com (cited), lightsonlab.com (cited) and the top results of the required search (iallpowers, Jackery and BLUETTI blogs, poweroutage.us). homepowerfacts has runtimes for 50 stations at an estimated 347 W (5,000 ÷ CEER 14.4) and list prices. It uses estimated usable Wh and has no measured delivered Wh, no weight figures and no solar refill times. lightsonlab works its runtimes from an assumed 225 W average for a 5,000 BTU unit. It says only that '800–1,200 W of panels can offset a small window AC in midday sun' and gives no refill hours for any kit. Neither page uses a measured delivered-Wh and recharge-Wh pair, and neither works out refill hours from the panels sold with a kit.
decides: Confirms the BLUETTI Elite 300 as the pick on measured numbers: 2.67 kWh delivered covers an 8-hour night at 50% duty (1,820 Wh) with about 850 Wh to spare. It does not cover a flat-out night (3,640 Wh). For a second night on solar, the Elite 300 + 2×200 W kit ($1,699) is not enough. Shoppers need about 1,200 W of panels (the Elite 300's maximum input), or a campground hookup. The R4000 is sold out at the maker today, so it can't be the lead pick.

findings.label: 5,000 BTU window AC flat-out draw (derived)
findings.source_title: Frigidaire 5,000 BTU 115 V White Window-Mounted Room Air Conditioner - FFRA051WAE (Abt)
findings.note: Abt lists the FFRA051WAE at 5,000 BTU and CEER 11, 115 V. 5,000 BTU/h ÷ 11 BTU/Wh = 455 W. CEER includes standby, so the steady compressor draw is a little higher. Abt says the item is no longer available. Frigidaire's own spec-sheet PDF did not render as text.

findings.label: Energy for one 8-hour night
findings.value: 3,640 Wh flat out; 1,820 Wh at 50% compressor duty
findings.note: 8 h × 455 W = 3,640 Wh. 8 h × 227.5 W = 1,820 Wh. The 50% duty cycle is an assumption, not a measurement.

findings.label: Price (maker US store)
findings.value: $1,199; $1,699 with 2×200 W panels; $2,048 with a 500 W panel
findings.note: Read from the Shopify store data. All three listings are in stock. The kit listings are bluettipower.com/products/elite-300-2-200w and /elite-300-500w.

findings.label: Measured energy delivered, full discharge
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 300 review: 3,014Wh, 2,400W and an 8ms UPS switchover in a 58-pound box (StorageReview)
findings.note: StorageReview measured 'a total draw of 2.67 kWh before the battery was fully depleted' at the output. 2,670 ÷ 3,014 = 0.89.

findings.label: Hours on a 5,000 BTU AC
findings.value: 5.9 h flat out; 11.7 h at 50% duty
findings.note: 2,670 Wh ÷ 455 W = 5.9 h. 2,670 ÷ 227.5 W = 11.7 h. An 8-hour flat-out night falls 970 Wh short (3,640 − 2,670).

findings.label: Cost per delivered Wh
findings.note: $1,199 ÷ 2,670 Wh = $0.45. $1,699 ÷ 2,670 Wh = $0.64. The 2,670 Wh is StorageReview's measurement.

findings.label: Delivered Wh per lb
findings.note: StorageReview spec table gives 26.3 kg (57.98 lb). 2,670 Wh ÷ 57.98 lb = 46 Wh/lb.

findings.label: Solar refill hours after one full discharge
findings.value: 8.7 h at 400 W (2×200 W kit); 7.0 h at 500 W; 2.9 h at the 1,200 W maximum input
findings.note: StorageReview measured 3.49 kWh of input for a 0–100% charge, and its spec table gives 1,200 W max solar input at 12–60 V. 3,490 ÷ 400 = 8.7 h. 3,490 ÷ 500 = 7.0 h. 3,490 ÷ 1,200 = 2.9 h. These are hours at full rated panel output. Real sun gives less, so refill times run longer. The 3.49 kWh was measured on wall charging; solar MPPT losses may differ.

findings.label: Price and availability (maker US store)
findings.value: $1,499 (compare-at $3,299), sold out; R4000 + SP037 400 W kit $1,798, sold out
findings.note: Read from the Shopify store data, which shows available: false. The kit is at iallpowers.com/products/allpowers-r4000-solar-generator-4000w-3600wh-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels.

findings.label: Hours on a 5,000 BTU AC (derived)
findings.value: 6.5 h flat out; 12.9 h at 50% duty
findings.note: Store text: 3,456 Wh, 4,000 W (6,000 W surge), 2,000 W max solar input. Usable energy is assumed at 85%, not measured: 3,456 × 0.85 = 2,938 Wh. 2,938 ÷ 455 = 6.5 h. 2,938 ÷ 227.5 = 12.9 h.

findings.label: Cost per usable Wh and refill from its kit panel (derived)
findings.value: $0.51/Wh; 7.3 h of full-rated 400 W output to refill 2,938 Wh, before charge losses
findings.note: $1,499 ÷ 2,938 Wh = $0.51. 2,938 ÷ 400 W = 7.3 h. At the 2,000 W maximum input: 2,938 ÷ 2,000 = 1.5 h. Both units are sold out today.
